report.source_text: We treated with rifabutin 300 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. Due to liver dysfunction 1 month after starting the treatment, the regimen was changed to moxifloxacin 400 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. Three months later, the patient developed nausea due to moxifloxacin. The treatment was then switched to linezolid 1200 mg/day and clarithromycin. Following these changes, there were no further complications, and the skin findings demonstrated a trend of improvement. The nodule flattened, and the postinflammatory pigmentation had faded over 7 months

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old aquarium worker developed chronic skin nodules and an ulcer on his right forearm and thumb following an arm injury about two years prior. Initial biopsy three months ago was negative for mycobacteria by culture and PCR. Subsequent cultures from a second biopsy grew colonies on Ogawa medium by day 11, with PCR sequencing confirming M. marinum. Histopathology of the second biopsy showed moderate inflammatory cell infiltration without granulomas or necrosis. MRI showed increased fat tissue density without abscess or osteomyelitis. The patient was treated with multiple antibiotics over 7 months with clinical improvement including flattening of the nodule and fading pigmentation.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Chronic skin nodules and ulcer following aquarium-related arm injury
Initial biopsy 3 months ago had negative cultures and PCR
Subsequent cultures positive for M. marinum confirmed by PCR sequencing
Histopathology showed moderate inflammatory cell infiltration without granulomas or necrosis
MRI showed increased fat tissue density but no abscess or osteomyelitis
Treatment with rifabutin, clarithromycin, then moxifloxacin, then linezolid and clarithromycin resulted in clinical improvement over 7 months
